D007-D015_h001.question:
"Honestly, doctor, it's been a rough seven months. I just feel… dead inside, like my emotions have been completely switched off. Things that used to excite me, like landing a big freelance gig, just leave me cold now. It’s hard to even get out of bed some days. I wake up hours before my alarm, around 3 AM, and just lie there, my mind racing but my body feeling so heavy, like I’m moving through molasses. Work has become a nightmare; I can barely focus, and I’m definitely not performing like I used to.

The really bizarre stuff started about a month before the depression really hit its peak. For the past six months, I’ve been having these… experiences. I’ll be trying to explain something, and my thoughts just jump all over the place; one moment I’m talking about servers, the next about my ex-wife’s cat, with no real connection. And I see things – shadows, figures in my peripheral vision that vanish when I turn directly, or sometimes full-blown images, usually of people watching me. It’s like everyone is talking about me, or these news reports have secret messages just for me in them. The weirdest part is, I’ve had these hallucinations and had these strange beliefs about people’s intentions for weeks now, even when I wasn't feeling particularly down or numb at all."
D007-D015_h001.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007-D015_h002.question:
It’s been a rough seven months, Doc. Mostly, I just feel… heavy. Like there’s a lead weight in my chest. Nothing really sparks joy anymore, not even watching the game, and I used to live for that. My wife, bless her heart, tries to get me to talk, but sometimes it feels like my tongue is stuck. Just getting the words out is a struggle.

And then there's the other stuff. For the last six months, it’s like my own personal nightmare. I keep seeing things, shadowy figures lurking in the corners of my workshop, sometimes even my dad, who passed years ago, just standing there watching me. And my wife… I know it sounds crazy, but I just have this unshakable feeling she’s cheating on me. I’ve gone through her phone, checked her mileage, even followed her once. I know it sounds absurd, but it's like a drill bit in my head, constantly turning. What’s even stranger, about a month ago, the heavy feeling started to lift a bit, but those figures were still there, and the thoughts about my wife were just as strong. It was a good two, maybe three weeks, feeling a little lighter emotionally, but the other stuff didn’t go away at all. That’s why I finally came in, I guess. I never sleep through the night anymore, and my head feels like scrambled eggs sometimes, making it hard to even explain all this.
D007-D015_h002.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007-D015_h003.question:
It’s been a rough seven months, Doc. This sadness… it just hangs over me like a thick cloud. Nothing brings me joy anymore, not even creating a new dish in the kitchen, which used to be my biggest thrill. My staff has noticed I’m moving slower, constantly dragging my feet. And no matter how exhausted I am, I’m always waking up before the sun, feeling just as tired as when I went to bed.

Things started to get really strange about six months ago. Before this deep sadness completely took over, there was a good two or three weeks where I was still feeling okay, quite energized actually. During that time, I started to believe I had a special gift, a sort of culinary genius that allowed me to taste combinations no one else could. I also kept smelling burnt sugar, even when there was nothing cooking in the kitchen. Now, that burnt sugar smell is constantly there, even with the sadness, and my thoughts jump around so much when I try to explain it all, making it hard to follow a single train of thought. It feels like my brain is moving at a hundred miles an hour, but my body is stuck in slow motion.
D007-D015_h003.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007-D015_h004.question:
It's been about seven months now that I’ve been feeling this deep, heavy sadness that just won't lift. Nothing brings me joy anymore, not even sketching, which used to be my escape. I just feel… empty. And the nightmares, they're constant and terrifying, leaving me exhausted even after a full night’s sleep. Lately, when people talk to me, it’s like my brain just can’t keep up, so I don’t respond right away.

This started around seven months ago, but about a month into it, things got really weird. I started seeing things—shadowy figures in my peripheral vision, and sometimes fully formed people who aren't really there. My thoughts also feel jumbled, like the words don't connect, and sometimes what comes out just sounds like a bunch of random words. The strange thing is, even when I'm not feeling so down, like for about a month now, those visual hallucinations and the feeling that I have some secret power, that I'm meant for something extraordinary, they still bother me. It's like they're just... always there, independently of my mood.
D007-D015_h004.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007-D015_h005.question:
It's a relief to finally be here. Honestly, I'm not even sure where to begin. For the past seven months, it’s been this relentless sadness, just a dark cloud that won't lift. I used to love my job as a pharmacist, helping people, but now, the thought of facing another day... it’s just a void. Nothing brings me joy anymore. My husband tries, but I just can’t feel it. I wake up at 3 AM every single day, my mind racing, and I can't fall back asleep. When someone asks me a question, it's like my brain has to wade through mud to even form a response.

And then there are these other things. For about six months now, these bizarre thoughts started creeping in. I keep seeing things out of the corner of my eye – shadows, fleeting figures that aren't there. And I'm convinced the world is ending, that a major catastrophe is coming and there's nothing anyone can do. Sometimes, when I try to talk about it, words come out that don't make sense, like "flumphing" or "glarble." My husband looks at me like I'm crazy.

The really confusing part is there was a stretch, about three weeks or so, where I was just feeling this impending doom, seeing those shadows and hearing my own made-up words, but the deep, soul-crushing sadness and not being able to feel anything, that wasn't there during that time. It came back, and it's been intense for months now, but those other things, they were there by themselves for a bit. It’s hard to keep it all straight.
D007-D015_h005.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007-D015_h006.question:
It’s been, well, forever, it feels like. Over a year and a half now, I think. Almost two years since I really felt like myself. I just… I don't care about anything anymore. My work, which I used to love – the intricate dance of flavors, the stories behind each vintage – it all feels so hollow. I’ve dropped a lot of weight because food just has no appeal. I feel this constant, gnawing emptiness inside, and my mind just keeps replaying every little misstep I’ve ever made, telling me how useless I am. It's like I'm stuck in a loop of guilt.

But then there are the other things, the things that are harder to explain. For about a year and four months now, I’ve been hearing voices. They tell me… they tell me I have a special gift, a deeper understanding of the universe, far beyond what anyone else comprehends. And for a good couple of weeks, even when the crushing sadness lifted for a bit, or at least wasn't as intense, those voices and the certainty of my special power, they didn't go away. They were still there, clear as day, without any of the gloom. Sometimes my thoughts get so jumbled, the words just don't come out right, like my brain is trying to speak a different language. It’s been really tough.
D007-D015_h006.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D007-D015_h007.question:
"I'm really struggling, doctor. It's been over a year now, probably closer to a year and seven months, that I've felt this crushing sadness. Nothing brings me joy anymore, not even my students who used to be the light of my life. I barely eat, and when I do, everything tastes like ash, like the world is decaying from the inside out. I feel so guilty all the time, responsible for things that aren't my fault, like I did something to cause all this… this 'gloobel' (I know, silly word, but it just feels right).

But it's more than just the sadness. For about a year and four months now, things have gotten really strange. Sometimes, I can actually taste that ashiness even when I haven't eaten anything, it's so vivid. And I have these really disturbing thoughts that the world is ending, that everything is just going to crumble into dust. It feels so real, like a catastrophe is just around the corner.

What's really unsettling, though, is that sometimes, even when I'm not feeling that deep, dark sadness, when I might have a slightly better day mood-wise, those terrifying thoughts about the world ending and that awful taste are still there. It’s like they linger, on their own, for a couple of weeks at a time, even when the depression might have eased up a bit. It’s not just tied to being super depressed, if that makes sense. It’s like they have their own life."
D007-D015_h007.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D007-D015_h008.question:
"I'm here because… well, things just aren't right. For over a year and a half now, I've felt this heavy cloud hanging over me. Most days I just feel incredibly down, and nothing brings me joy anymore. My husband tries to get me to do things we used to love, like gardening or even just watching a movie, but I just can't find the interest. And my appetite has been way up – I’m constantly eating, which isn't like me. I ruminate constantly about little mistakes from years ago at work, feeling this crushing guilt I can’t shake. It's gotten so bad that sometimes I'll say things that just pop into my head, words that only make sense to me, like 'quantifry' when I mean to say 'quantify.'

What's really disturbing, though, are these other things happening. For the past year and four months, I've been seeing things, shadowy figures at the edges of my vision, and I'm convinced that the news anchors on TV are sending me secret messages through their gestures, specifically for me. This has been going on about as long as the depression. But there was a stretch, about three weeks last summer, where I was feeling a bit better – not happy, but not completely sunk – and yet, those shadowy figures were still there, and the news anchors were still trying to communicate with me. That’s what makes me think it’s more than just the depression; these visions and messages stick around even when my mood lifts a little."
D007-D015_h008.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D007-D015_h009.question:
It's been about a year and seven months now that I’ve felt this constant heaviness. There's just no point to anything. What’s the use of me operating this crane, building anything, when it all feels so meaningless? I used to take such pride in my work, in providing for my wife, but now, even big projects finishing just leave me flat. Honestly, I've put on a good 15 pounds in the last couple of months; I just can't stop eating.

What really gets to me, though, is this crushing guilt. I know it sounds crazy, but I’m convinced that somehow, I’m responsible for all the recent delays on our job site, even the ones that are clearly due to weather. I keep hearing this specific woman’s voice, from a couple of projects back, whispering that she’s in love with me, that she’s watching me. And then there are other voices, too, sometimes saying things that don't even make sense, these weird, jumbled words that only I seem to understand. It’s been going on for over a year now, closer to sixteen months.

The strangest part – and this is really what's throwing off my wife – is that there was definitely a period, for a good three weeks or so, where all I had was the voices and that woman's voice telling me she loved me. No sadness, no guilt, no feeling down, just those experiences. But then the dark mood always creeps back in eventually and stays for ages, swallowing everything else. It makes it impossible to do my job right; I can barely focus.
D007-D015_h009.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D007-D015_h010.question:
"It's been a really tough year and a half, doctor, maybe even longer. I think my husband, Mark, made the appointment because he's been so worried. For about a year and seven months now, I just haven't been myself. Running the franchise, something I used to pour my heart into, feels meaningless. I’ve lost all interest in it, and even our weekly dinner dates, which I always looked forward to, now just feel like a chore. I've been so tearful, just crying for no reason, and I've dropped a lot of weight – about 15 pounds in the last month – without even trying. I keep feeling this crushing guilt, like somehow, I’m responsible for the local restaurant down the street having to close, even though Mark says it’s ridiculous.

But it’s not just the sadness. For the last year and four months, I've also been hearing things, whispers mostly, and sometimes full sentences when no one's there. And everything feels like it’s about me. The news reports, snippets of conversation from strangers, even the lyrics on the radio – it all seems to have a hidden message meant just for me. The oddest thing is, there was a stretch, about three weeks in the middle of last year, where those voices and the feeling that everything was connected to me were still happening, even though I actually felt pretty okay and wasn’t feeling down or guilty at all during that time. Then the depression came back with a vengeance. Right now, it's all happening together. The voices and the sadness."
D007-D015_h010.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D007-D015_h011.question:
Lately, things have been… really off. It’s been about seven months now. I’m finding it impossible to enjoy anything, even playing with my kids, which used to be all I looked forward to. I just feel this crushing guilt all the time about things I can’t even pinpoint, like I’ve done something terrible. I pace the house for hours, can’t sit still, and I even tried to… well, I made an attempt a few weeks ago because I just couldn't take it anymore.

The thing is, it’s more than just feeling down. I've been feeling these strange crawling sensations under my skin, like bugs, and I know they're not real. And the news reports, the way people look at me – it all feels like it’s specifically about me, like they’re sending me messages. It makes it hard to focus, and sometimes when my wife asks me something, my mind just goes off on its own tangent, and I can't quite answer her directly. I've even found myself laughing at incredibly inappropriate times, like a silly kid, and I don't know why.

For the most part, these feelings, this deep sadness and the strange things like the skin crawling, they happen all at the same time. But what's really confusing is that there was a period, about three weeks last month, where I was feeling a bit better, not so low, but those crawling sensations and the feeling that the news was talking to me – those stuck around quite strongly even when I wasn't in that deep funk. It's like the wired thoughts just continued on their own.
D007-D015_h011.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007-D015_h012.question:
It’s been almost seven months now, and honestly, I just can’t shake this feeling. Everything feels… pointless. I used to love planning weddings, seeing the joy on couples’ faces, but now, it’s like everything is crashing down. I hear voices sometimes, whispering about how the world is ending, how a huge catastrophe is coming. It’s terrifying. I even started saying these strange words, "gloaming-shards" or "void-song," and only I know what they mean.

There are also times when I just freeze, my movements feeling incredibly slow, like I’m moving through thick mud. I'll make these weird faces without even realizing it. Even things I used to enjoy, like my husband’s cooking or our weekly movie night, just… there’s nothing there. No pleasure. I feel so worthless, like a burden. Lately, I've had these terrifying urges, like wanting to jump in front of a car when I’m out walking, even though I don't want to die.

The strangest part is, for a couple of weeks there, after a really bad depressive spell lifted a bit, I was still hearing the voices loud and clear, and getting those strong feelings about the world ending. The sadness and the slowness weren’t as intense, but the voices and the feeling of doom were definitely still there, even without the low mood. Then everything came crashing back down, and now it feels like both the voices and the depression are constantly present.
D007-D015_h012.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007-D015_h013.question:
"It's been a rough seven months, Doc. Mostly, I just feel… worthless. Like a burden on my late wife's memory. I don't see the point in doing much, and I find myself picking at my cuticles constantly, or pacing the living room for no reason. I’ve started avoiding my old fishing buddies – just don’t have the energy for it. Sometimes, I get these sudden, terrifying urges, like to just step right into traffic, or jump off the old bridge near my house, even though I don't really want to die.

And I'm tasting something metallic all the time, even when I haven't eaten anything. It messes with my words sometimes too, everything gets jumbled, like "the sky is purple and the cat sings the ocean's blue." The oddest thing, though, is sometimes I can't help but copy how other people move, like when the nurse adjusted her pen, I found myself doing the exact same thing a moment later. It's like I'm not entirely in control, even when the sadness isn't overwhelming me."
D007-D015_h013.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007-D015_h014.question:
"It's been a rough seven months, Doc. I just feel… heavy, all the time. Getting out of bed for my subway shifts feels like lifting a train car. My wife, bless her, says I just sit there staring sometimes, and yeah, I do. My mind’s just blank. When I do talk, it's like my words are stuck, like pushing through thick mud. And the guilt… it’s crushing. Everything is my fault. The thought of just not being here anymore crosses my mind pretty often, though I wouldn’t do anything.

And then there are these words, they just pop into my head, like 'chufflegrip' or 'shimmerwallow.' They make sense to me, but I know they don't to anyone else. It's like my body gets stuck too, sometimes; I'll just stand there, frozen, in the middle of doing something.

What's really strange, though, is that even when I have a few days where the sadness lifts a bit, those strange feelings, like being watched and the crawling sensations, they don't disappear. They were there for a good two, maybe three weeks, even before this deep cloud of depression settled over me, and they still pop up sometimes even when I'm not feeling completely down. It’s like they have a life of their own, separate from the blues."
D007-D015_h014.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
